subject: Clearpoint PO XML requirements & weekly statement exception
messages:
From: Megan Soto <megan.soto@clearpoint.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@clearpoint.com
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: PO XML schema & weekly statement exception for Clearpoint SOW

Hi Jordan,

We're finalizing procurement for the Redwood deployment and I need to confirm a few mandatory items from our end before legal signs off. Our AP system requires the following for every invoice: a machine-readable PO XML that includes a top-level purchaseOrderId attribute and a lineItems array where each line item has a skuId, quantity, and unitPrice. We also need the invoice to reference the PO ID in the invoice header so our ERPs can auto-match.

Two procurement constraints to flag:
- Net terms: Standard preference is net45, but we can be flexible if the billing cadence changes.
- Invoice cadence: Our treasury team requires weekly statement uploads (every Monday) for high-volume SaaS vendors rather than monthly statements. This is non-standard for us but required when multiple internal cost centers hit the same vendor. Can Redwood accommodate weekly statements and map PO lineItems to our ERP line codes?

If you can accept weekly statements, we may need an exception document (signed amendment) that notes consolidated monthly reconciliation will still be performed. I attached a sample PO export so you can see the XML schema we require.

Thanks,
Megan Soto
Procurement Manager, Clearpoint Systems
[Attachment: Clearpoint_PO_template.xml (application/xml)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Megan Soto <megan.soto@clearpoint.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO XML schema & weekly statement exception for Clearpoint SOW

Hi Megan — thanks for the detail and the sample XML.

We can support a PO XML import and map purchaseOrderId + lineItems to our billing metadata. Two operational notes:
1) Weekly statements: We can generate weekly statement files on Mondays and include a PO ID header for each invoice line. However, weekly statements increase billing ops and reconciliation overhead on our side.
2) Pricing/discount impact: The current commercial for CPX-00123 includes an early-pay discount (2% for net30). If we move to a weekly statement model that materially increases handling, finance will likely require adjusting that discount or moving to net30 to cover the extra ops.

Proposed compromise: Redwood will accept weekly statements for the first 90 days with the following conditions:
- Customer accepts net30 for that period (instead of net45).
- We establish a consolidated monthly reconciliation file (we still provide weekly statements, but month-end will reconcile).
- We include a small one-time onboarding credit to offset any mapping work.

I've attached a short guidance doc on how we consume PO XMLs and the preferred field mapping. If that works, we'll produce an amendment to the SOW and route it for signature (DocuSign link in the cover sheet).

Deal: CPX-00123
Next step: Can you confirm whether Clearpoint can move to net30 for the initial 90-day weekly-statement pilot? If yes, we'll draft the amendment.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198
[Attachment: PO_acceptance_guidance.pdf (application/pdf)]

Looping finance/ops in — a couple of product/packaging questions before we commit: 

- Mapping: Can our billing system persist the Clearpoint ERP line code on each usage line so it shows up in the invoice XML exactly as they provided? We need this for downstream chargeback.
- Packaging/discounts: If we accept weekly statements and move to net30 for the pilot, do we automatically lose the early-pay discount? I want to be explicit so account team isn't blindsided during renewal.
- Operational cost: Weekly statements will increase bill frequency and reconciliation time. Can we negotiate a small one-time credit (~$2k) or a short-term rev share offset to compensate?

Ben — finance: can you confirm whether we can support weekly weekly-statement processing and what pre-auth or holdback you'd need to feel comfortable (if any)?

If finance can support it under clear mitigations, I'm ok to offer the 90-day pilot and include an explicit clause that moves billing to monthly after the pilot unless Clearpoint requests otherwise.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO XML schema & weekly statement exception for Clearpoint SOW

Short answer: finance can operationally support weekly statements, but we need risk protection. Proposed terms from Finance: 
- Move to net30 for the 90-day weekly-statement pilot (shortens the receivable window).
- Require a pre-authorization hold equal to 20% of Clearpoint's estimated monthly spend (applied to a hold account); releases on reconciliation.
- Offer a one-time operational credit of $2,250 to offset integration mapping work.

Operational play: accept weekly statements for 90 days, run month-end consolidated reconciliation, then transition to monthly statements unless Clearpoint elects to stay on weekly and pays a nominal monthly handling fee.

If legal approves the amendment language, finance is good to proceed.

-Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

- We'll move to net30 for the 90-day pilot.
- We agree to the 20% pre-authorization hold; treasury will provide the funding profile.
- We accept the one-time $2,250 onboarding credit against the first invoice.
- Weekly statements on Mondays are acceptable; we'll expect a consolidated monthly reconciliation file at month-end.

Please go ahead and send the SOW amendment and DocuSign link. Once the amendment is signed, procurement will issue the first machine-readable PO referencing purchaseOrderId CPX-PO-4592.
